items.stem: A test returns p = 0.03 with alpha set at 0.05. What is the correct conclusion?

options.text: The result is statistically significant at the 0.05 level; reject the null hypothesis
options.rationale: Correct: p is below alpha, so you reject the null at that level.

options.text: The null hypothesis is proven true
options.rationale: Hypothesis tests never prove the null; they fail to reject or reject it.

options.text: There is a 3% chance the alternative is false
options.rationale: A p-value is not the probability that a hypothesis is true or false.

options.text: The effect is definitely large and important
options.rationale: Significance speaks to detectability, not to the practical size of the effect.

items.explanation: Correct: p is below alpha, so you reject the null at that level.

items.stem: Which statements about a 95% confidence interval for a mean are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: Over many repeated samples, about 95% of such intervals would contain the true mean
options.rationale: Correct: the 95% refers to the long-run capture rate of the procedure.

options.text: A larger sample size tends to produce a narrower interval
options.rationale: Correct: more data reduces the standard error and narrows the interval.

options.text: There is a 95% probability the true mean lies in this specific interval
options.rationale: The parameter is fixed; the 95% describes the procedure, not this one interval.

options.text: The interval always contains the sample mean's opposite value
options.rationale: This is not a meaningful property of a confidence interval.

items.explanation: Correct: the 95% refers to the long-run capture rate of the procedure.

items.stem: Ice-cream sales and drowning incidents are positively correlated. What most likely explains this?

options.text: A confounding variable, hot weather, drives both
options.rationale: Correct: a common cause (hot weather) produces the association without direct causation.
There is no plausible direct causal mechanism; a confounder is the likely cause.
This reverses an implausible causal claim and still ignores the confounder.

options.text: The correlation must be a calculation error
options.rationale: The correlation is real; it is explained by a confounder, not an error.

items.explanation: Correct: a common cause (hot weather) produces the association without direct causation.
